title: Canary exit criteria and rollback scenarios (personal notebook)
content:
Context / purpose:
- Quick personal notes for running model and infra canaries. This is not the canonical runbook yet — meant to capture heuristics I use when I own a rollout window.
- Focus: clear binary exit criteria (go/no-go), fast rollback triggers, and a lightweight progression plan that SRE/owners can follow without reading the full runbook.

High-level approach (heuristic):
1) Start very small (0.5% of traffic) for 20–30m steady window.
2) If golden signals are green, increase to 5% for 40–60m.
3) If still green and QA smoke tests pass, shift to 20% for 1–2h.
4) Final ramp to 100% (or target) in 2–3 steps dependent on traffic patterns.

Primary metrics to watch (golden signals + quality probes):
- p95 latency (in ms) — baseline + 20% absolute cap for canary.
- error rate (4xx/5xx) — absolute threshold 0.5% for canary; relative increase >2x = immediate pause.
- CPU/GPU utilization & queue depth — unexpected spikes = caution.
- OOM/crash counts — any crash => immediate rollback.
- Token cost anomalies (tokens per response) — +15% unexplained => investigate.
- Delta in embedding distances (for embedding model swaps) on golden subset — >10% drift flagged.
- Human eval sample passrate on 200 random sessions (quick sample) — drop >4% => rollback.

Exit criteria (succeed):
- No threshold breaches during the observation window AND
- All smoke tests pass (end-to-end CLI + integration tests) AND
- No customer-facing incidents or PagerDuty alerts raised by autosystems.

Immediate rollback triggers (automated/manual):
- Any new 5xx spike >0.2% absolute in 10m window.
- P95 latency > baseline * 1.5 for more than 15m.
- Model output quality signal from evals: drop >4% on golden set after 1000 tokens sampled.
- Crash/OOM on serving nodes.
- Unexplained increases in tokens/cost or hallucination rate flagged by regression detector.

Rollback mechanics (practical steps):
- API-level quick revert: route traffic back to previous pinned version via Traffic Manager UI or: curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/router/reweight -d '{"route":"my-route","from":"v2.1.3-canary","to":"v2.1.2"}' (ops token required).
- If routing not responsive: scale down canary pool in infra console (dedicated) or remove canary nodes.
- Notify: #releases channel, on-call, and affected product PMs. Template message: "Rolling back canary v2.1.3 -> v2.1.2 due to [metric]. ETA to revert: ~2–8min."
- Post-rollback: run sanity smoke tests and leave canary disabled until root cause triage.

Pinning conventions / naming notes (so you can find the safe version quickly):
- Use semver + bake tag: <model>-v<semver>-<bakeYYYYMMDD>-<owner initials> e.g. llama-fox-v1.7.2-bake20250902-pa
- Keep a quick mapping in the release ticket body to previous stable candidate(s).

Observability checklist (what I open right away):
- Serving runtime dashboard (per model route): p50/p95/p99, errors, request rate.
- Deployment tracing: request_id->node mapping (to identify hot nodes).
- Token distribution chart (tokens per request over time).
- Automated canary regression alerts (ML eval service) for semantic drift on top-10 prompts.
- Kibana/Logs: tail the canary nodes for stack traces, retry storms.

Smoke tests (quick set to run at each stage):
- CLI smoke: 6 scripted prompts with expected outputs (sanity assertions).
- Latency smoke: synthetic 100 QPS for 2m, verify p95 within threshold.
- E2E: run 5 typical user flows (uploads, summarize, rerank) on canary route.

Progression script (manual checklist):
- [ ] Stage 0: deploy canary artifact to pool (tagged)
- [ ] Stage 1: open 0.5% traffic, start 30m timer, check metrics every 5m
- [ ] Stage 2: if green -> 5% (40m), kick-off human eval sample (100 queries)
- [ ] Stage 3: if green -> 20% (1h), run full smoke + token-cost sanity
- [ ] Stage 4: decide to proceed to 100% or abort/rollback

Notes about automation and confidence scoring:
- If we have a reliable anomaly detector that outputs an "anomaly score" for combined signals, consider a soft auto-advance when score < 0.2 for entire stage. But I rarely trust full automation without an SRE thumbs-up.
- Consider flapping protection: require stability for two windows before final ramp if change is large (major model version, quant changes).

Troubleshooting quick hits:
- Latency without error spike: check KV-cache hit rates, tokenization differences, batching efficiency, and recent kernel selection logs.
- Increased token usage per request: check prompt template change, new system instruction, or model tokenizer differences.
- Quality drop but infra healthy: compare sampling seeds, decoding params, and confirm model weights (no accidental float->int quant mismatch).

Open questions / TODOs (for product/release discussion):
- What is the canonical sample size for human eval that teams accept? I use 200 but some folks insist on 500. Add to release policy.
- Should we require automated regression evaluation for every canary promotion (adds time but reduces surprises)?
- Make the routing revert endpoint part of the release ticket body (copyable).

Notes to self (personal):
- When on-call, be conservative. If you see a sign you don't fully understand, pause the ramp and call an engineer.
- During high traffic (US morning), favor smaller steps.
- Keep a short log in the release ticket: minute-by-minute notes are super helpful for postmortems.

Reference snippets (copy into ticket):
- Rollback message: "Action: rollback to v2.1.2. Trigger: p95 latency 1.7x baseline for 20m. Owner: Priya Anand. Incident notes: investigating GPU kernel mismatch."
- Quick command (replace tokens): curl -X POST $CONTROLPLANE/api/routes/reweight -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPSTOKEN" -d '{"route":"my-route","weights":{"v2.1.2":1.0}}'

End.
